https://nineoclock.ro/exim-banca-romanea.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Bucharest, August 4, 2026 – Exim Banca Românească is strengthening its position as a key financier of Romanian businesses by joining the consortium of banks that granted MOOV Leasing a €187 million syndicated loan, one of the most significant syndicated financings granted to an entrepreneurial company in Romania’s operational leasing sector. The new facility will support the company’s next stage of development, expanding access to operational leasing for SMEs and launching products dedicated to individual customers. The facility refinances the 110 million euro syndicated loan contracted by the company last year and increases MOOV’s financing capacity by more than 70%. The transaction was coordinated by UniCredit Bank, Banca Transilvania and Raiffeisen Bank, acting as Global Coordinators, Mandated Lead Arrangers (MLAs) and Co-Documentation Agents alongside ING Bank N.V. Amsterdam – Bucharest Branch and Exim Banca Românească, acting as Mandated Lead Arrangers. As part of the transaction, UniCredit SpA also acted as ESG Coordinator, Banca Transilvania as Facility Agent, and Raiffeisen Bank as Security Agent. Sustain LCM Finance, founded by Grația Annamaria Popescu, assisted MOOV in structuring and coordinating this syndicated financing, which also includes a sustainability-linked feature (SLL), providing specialized debt syndication advisory services throughout the entire syndication process. Legal advice on the transaction was provided by Filip & Company, for the lenders’ consortium, and by Stoica, Popa & Asociații, for MOOV. The facility is structured as a Sustainability-Linked Loan (SLL), a mechanism through which certain financing terms are linked to the achievement of environmental and social sustainability targets undertaken by the company. This structure reflects MOOV’s commitment to integrating ESG principles into its business development and to building a responsible growth model aligned with European best practices. The new facility will enable the company to accelerate the implementation of its growth strategy along three main directions: Accelerating SME financing by expanding access to modern and flexible mobility solutions; Launching operational leasing for individuals, offering retail customers a simple and predictable alternative to traditional car purchasing; Expanding the partner ecosystem by developing collaboration with importers and national car dealer networks, diversifying the offering available through the MOOV platform. Through this financing, the company is strengthening its capacity to respond to a market undergoing accelerated transformation, in which mobility is increasingly seen as a service, and vehicle usage is gaining ground over vehicle ownership. Mircea Dihel and Bogdan Speteanu , founders of MOOV Leasing: “The signing of this syndicated facility marks another important milestone in MOOV’s development. Increasing the financing ceiling from EUR 110 million to EUR 187 million confirms the confidence our banking partners place in our business model, execution capability, and the results we have achieved in recent years. The new facility gives us the resources needed to continue the accelerated development of the SME segment, as well as to take a natural step toward operational leasing for individuals. We aim to make access to mobility simpler, more transparent, and fully digital, offering customers a modern alternative to traditional car purchasing. At the same time, we will continue expanding our national partner network and developing the technology platform that underpins our business model.” Founded in 2022, MOOV is one of the fastest-growing companies in the Romanian operational leasing and mobility services market. The company operates through its proprietary digital platform, accessible both online and at partner dealer showrooms across the country, which simplifies the entire process, from vehicle selection to contract signing and management. In 2025, MOOV reported revenue of RON 189.9 million, more than double that of the previous year, while total assets reached RON 535.8 million, reflecting the company’s rapid growth and the consolidation of its market position. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Ryan Bridge asking a question of Reform UK’s leader, Nigel Farage, at the party’s conference in Birmingham on Saturday. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA View image in fullscreen Ryan Bridge asking a question of Reform UK’s leader, Nigel Farage, at the party’s conference in Birmingham on Saturday. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA UK news Raise the Colours leader given access to Reform UK conference while on bail Ryan Bridge, arrested this year on suspicion of religiously and racially aggravated harassment, says party invited him Ben Quinn Sat 5 Sep 2026 10.45 EDT Last modified on Sat 5 Sep 2026 11.52 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The leader of a flag campaign group who was arrested on suspicion of causing religiously and racially aggravated harassment was given access to Reform UK’s annual conference. Ryan Bridge, whose Raise the Colours group has put up hundreds of union and St George flags across England, told the Guardian he was invited to the conference. Raise the Colours has argued the campaign displays flags as a sign of patriotism, but it has been accused of using them to spread anti-immigrant sentiment. Raise the Colours co-founder Ryan Bridge attends Reform UK conference Bridge’s attendance at the event comes as Reform UK has been attempting to attract more wavering centre-ground voters who have been reluctant to support the party. But a threat from its hard-right rival Restore Britain has given the party reason to pull rightwards. At a conference event on Saturday, Nigel Farage paid tribute to the flag campaign and told Bridge personally that Reform UK would offer legal support. “What your campaign has done is wake up vast parts of this country,” Farage told Bridge from a stage inside the conference after the activist was among three people selected to ask questions of the Reform leader during a discussion hosted by Jeremy Kyle. “If we can help you legally, we will,” said Farage, after Bridge told him he had an injunction against him putting up flags in Oxfordshire and was also facing one from Birmingham city council. Bridge was among 10 activists who were banned from France this year after they travelled there to take part in actions intended to stop migrant boats embarking across the Channel. He is also named along with six other people in action pursued by Birmingham city council as it seeks a high court injunction to stop activists from Raise the Colours putting flags up. The first hearing of that application will be on Tuesday. Bridge has been on bail since Thames Valley police confirmed earlier this year that a 44-year-old male from Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, was arrested after reports of incidents of public order offences on Abingdon Road, Oxford. The force said he was arrested “on suspicion of causing racially and religiously aggravated harassment, alarm or distress” and that he had been released on police bail. Bridge denies all wrongdoing. He is also facing a trial in East Sussex. He entered a not guilty plea at Brighton magistrates court last month after being charged with common assault in relation to an incident in the city in June and was granted bail. Bridge told the Guardian at the Reform conference on the outskirts of Birmingham on Friday: “We have come to the event today in light of it’s in my home city of Birmingham and with what’s going on with Raise the Colours … what we are doing.” “We got an invite, so we thought we would come along,” he added, saying he was not a member of Reform. There are no general admission tickets to the Reform conference for members of the public. Conference attenders are almost entirely members, with the addition of some lobbyists, people with business interests, diplomatic representatives and members of the press. Commercial passes can be bought for £650 and “platinum” tickets can cost thousands. Asked if his arrests posed a problem with him being at the event, Bridge said: “Being accused of a criminal act of raising a flag of your country in your country, I think is lesser than the actual criminal act that is going on on a daily basis from the far-left ultra NGOs.” Reform UK did not respond when contacted about Bridge being at its conference. His attendance was criticised by the anti-fascist campaign group Hope Not Hate, which said: “That someone as extreme as Ryan Bridge was inside the Reform conference with a pass is genuinely shocking.” Explore more on these topics UK news news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://tribuneonlineng.com/russian-dron.text: A plane carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky was delayed in Moldova after a Russian drone entered the country’s airspace, forcing a temporary shutdown of flights. Zelensky and his wife, Olena, were at Chisinau International Airport preparing to fly to Norway for the funeral of King Harald V when the drone crossed into Moldovan airspace from the direction of Ukraine. The drone prompted authorities to close Moldova’s airspace, leaving Zelensky’s plane on the runway for about an hour. Three departures and four arrivals were also delayed, according to Moldovan government spokesman Dumitru Ciorici. The flight was allowed to leave after authorities confirmed that the drone had come down and exploded about 160km (100 miles) from Chisinau airport. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre had initially said Zelensky’s plane was “almost hit by a drone” while taking off. However, a Ukrainian source told AFP that the danger had been exaggerated. The Kremlin said there had been no threat to Zelensky’s plane. ALSO READ: Trump to give every adult American $5,000 if Republicans win midterms Zelensky and his wife eventually arrived safely in Oslo, where he held talks with Mr Støre and other officials about military aid for Ukraine. They later attended King Harald’s funeral before travelling to Iceland and then Canada for further talks. Moldova has increasingly been affected by Russia’s war in Ukraine. Russian drones have entered Moldovan airspace several times, with officials warning that the incidents are becoming more frequent. Ukraine has closed its own airspace to civilian flights since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Zelensky normally travels by train to Poland before taking flights to other countries. The latest incident comes as Russian drone attacks on Ukraine intensify. Kyiv has also carried out long-range drone strikes against targets inside Russia. Peace talks involving US President Donald Trump’s special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are continuing, but efforts to end the war have so far failed to produce an agreement. (BBC News)

https://www.politico.eu/article/spaniard.text: A wave of housing protests swept across dozens of Spanish cities on Saturday as Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez weighed calling a snap election. The largest demonstration took place in Madrid, where four columns of protesters filled the capital’s main boulevards before converging on Cibeles Square. The Spanish Tenants Union, which organized the protests, said 500,000 people took to the streets, while the government’s delegation in Madrid estimated 70,000 protesters participated. Spanish Tenants Union spokesperson Valeria Racu said the turnout reflected public exasperation with political leaders who have failed to tackle a housing crisis in which average rents have risen nearly 90% over the past decade. Advertisement Advertisement “The people on the streets once again hold the power,” she said while addressing the demonstration, insisting that their movement would “no longer tolerate inaction.” The protests were triggered after an investment firm evicted 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from the apartment where she had lived since 1956. Sánchez’s government sought to contain the discontent on Tuesday by unveiling two long-delayed bills aimed at curbing speculative practices, extending eviction protections for vulnerable tenants and automatically renewing existing contracts. But conservative lawmakers in parliament rejected both bills on Friday. Amid the defeat, senior government figures indicated Sánchez — already under pressure over the ongoing migrant crisis in Ceuta and corruption cases involving members of his family and close political allies — was considering calling a snap election in a bid to capitalize on anger over housing. Protesters hold a banner reading ‘towards the general strike’ along Gran Via street during a demonstration against the housing crisis on October 3, 2026 in Madrid. | Pablo Blazquez Dominguez/Getty Images Saturday’s protests underscored the risks of that strategy. While demonstrators slammed the conservative opposition for voting down the bills, they also accused Sánchez of failing to tackle the housing crisis since taking office in 2018. “Eight days of people power have achieved more than eight years of progressive government,” Racu said, adding that protesters would continue pressuring politicians “regardless of who governs this country.” Calling for a general strike to force the adoption of urgent housing measures, Racu said “the feelings of disaffection, desperation, disillusionment and sadness have been replaced by a new energy on the streets.” Advertisement Advertisement As the demonstrations took place, Sánchez remained out of sight, weighing his options. Emiliano García-Page, the Socialist president of Castilla-La Mancha, and the party’s leaders in Extremadura, the Basque Country and Castilla y León on Saturday urged Sánchez to call an early election, saying voters needed to be heard. Meanwhile, the prospect of an imminent election is prompting Spain’s fractured left to scramble to regroup. With Deputy Prime Minister Yolanda Díaz declining to run for reelection, Health Minister Mónica García and Culture Minister Ernest Urtasun are seen as frontrunners to succeed her in the leadership of the Sumar party. But Podemos leader Irene Montero is also positioning herself to lead a broader left-wing alliance. So, too, is longtime housing activist and former Barcelona Mayor Ada Colau, who has signaled a willingness to return to frontline politics at the head of a progressive coalition. The center-right People’s Party leads in electoral polls with 34% support and is open to forming a government with the far-right Vox party, which is polling at 18%. Sánchez’s Socialists are backed by 26% of voters, and would need the fragmented left to unite behind a viable electoral alliance capable of winning enough seats in parliament to form a fresh coalition. Spain’s housing protests have begun to spill beyond the country’s borders, with similar demonstrations held in Lisbon, Dublin, Potsdam and The Hague. The mobilizations reflect a bloc-wide crisis marked by the lack of affordable homes and governments under pressure to increase housing supply.

https://www.just-drinks.com/news/amber-l.text: Credit: Tanya Keisha / Shutterstock.com Amber Latvijas Balzams stayed in the red in the first half of its financial year as lower sales volumes continued to weigh on its business. In its unaudited results for the first six months of 2026, the company, which is central to financial issues at the wider Amber Beverage Group, booked a loss of €0.95m ($1m). Find out more That compared with a €1.2m profit in the same period of last year, a financial statement from the business said yesterday (30 September). The group moved into the red in its first quarter results, which were shared in June . Amber Latvijas Balzams’ net revenue declined 30.4% in the period to €24.6m. Total sales volumes, measured in 9-litre cases, fell 38.2% year on year. The company attributed the contraction “mainly” to “declining consumption and purchasing power in the Baltic States and other markets, increases in excise duty rates, as well as a decline in contract manufacturing orders.” Volumes in the Baltic markets declined 34% in the period, while contract manufacturing volumes dropped 28%. The business also cited “lower export orders” from Stoli Group companies, mainly in the US. Sales of the Stoli and Elit brands fell 35% in the first half, the release said. Stoli is owned by SPI Group Holding, a “major” shareholder in Amber Beverage Group. Amber Latvijas Balzams generated gross profit of €2.9m during the period, down 56.5%, driven by lower volumes and changes to its pricing methodology. In February, a Riga court approved “ legal protection proceedings ” for Amber Latvijas Balzams to restructure its liabilities due to intense cash-flow pressures. It stemmed from “external challenges”, including disruptions at Stoli’s US business , Amber Latvijas Balzams’ largest customer, which left the Latvian manufacturer unable to meet creditor payments. The court has since extended the deadline for the company to secure approval for its restructuring “action plan” from June 5 to October 5. Meanwhile, Amber Beverage Group, which owns just under 90% of Amber Latvijas Balzams, entered its own “judicial reorganisation proceedings” in April. The move followed a formal event of default in February when the group failed to repay bondholders within a 20-business-day window. In April, the Moskovskaya vodka owner secured a moratorium on its debt obligations, which in August was extended to 24 December. The proceedings look to help Amber Beverage reach an “amicable” agreement with creditors or get approval for a formal regorganisation plan. Amber Latvijas Balzams says it is “the largest producer” of alcohlic drinks in the Baltics. It operates two production sites in Riga, where is makes strong alcoholic spirits, sparkling wine brands and “lighter” alcoholic drinks.
